subject: Dedicated capacity saturation — continuity playbook & next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@atlas-retail.com>, Atlas Retail Ops <ops@atlas-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — initial continuity playbook & asks

Claire / Atlas Ops team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. I wanted to follow up with a concise package and concrete asks so we can move from incident triage to a stable bridge and commercial close.

Summary of what we observed (from your report + our telemetry):
- Brief saturation window: ~08:42–09:03 PT affecting your US-dedicated pool (approx 3.5k concurrent inference streams).
- Latency spike and queued tokens; automatic autoscaler did not add warm nodes fast enough for peak fanout.
- No data exfiltration suspected; request paths remained internal to the tenant pool.

Attached: atlas_evidence_package.zip (logs + scheduler traces) and an initial continuity playbook (redwood_continuity_playbook_v1.pdf).

Immediate asks for Atlas Ops:
1) Can you confirm whether client-side fallback to the smaller model was observed or blocked? (ops@)
2) Please pull any gateway logs for 08:30–09:15 PT and share the head request IDs you see; we included our matching IDs in the evidence package.
3) Is procurement asking us to propose a commercial bridge (credits / short-term reserve) while we deploy the playbook? If yes, flag to me and Ben — we’ll prepare a term sheet.

Our proposed next steps (actionable, timeboxed):
- Today EOD: Redwood will deliver a runnable canary of the playbook and a testing checklist. (Owner: Marissa)
- 24–48h: Run a canary in your non-prod environment and validate autoscaler warmup times. (Owner: Atlas Ops + Redwood SRE)
- 72h: If canary succeeds, schedule a staged rollout with traffic ramping (Owner: Ben / Marissa).

I’ll send an internal action matrix in line with our commitments and then a consolidated note for signature on a limited commercial bridge if that helps close timelines.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachments: atlas_evidence_package.zip, redwood_continuity_playbook_v1.pdf
From: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@atlas-retail.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Retail Ops <ops@atlas-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:35:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — initial continuity playbook & asks

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. Quick answers:
- We did have client-side fallbacks enabled but they appear to have throttled due to an upstream gateway retry loop; we are pulling that trace now.
- We attached the head request IDs to a secured ticket (ID 4237); ops@ pushed a partial log bundle to the same S3 share you referenced.
- Procurement wants an interim commercial solution — not full reserved capacity yet, but they want a credit for the degradation window while the playbook is validated.

Can you give us an example credit amount or a ballpark so we can align with procurement expectations? Also want to confirm there was no request rerouting outside the tenant pool.

—
Claire Dunn
Director of Platform Engineering, Atlas Retail
claire.dunn@atlas-retail.com
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Atlas saturation — action matrix + proposal (please review)

Team,

Notes from Claire below. I pulled our runbook and drafted a short action matrix and a commercial term suggestion. Please review inline and call out anything you disagree with before I send Atlas the consolidated note.

Action matrix (owners + target SLA):
- Evidence handoff & mutual logs: Owner: Marissa (complete within 4h). Deliverable: sanitized log package and scheduler traces.
- Canary playbook + checklist: Owner: Marissa (deliver today EOD). Deliverable: playbook PDF + test plan.
- Autoscaler warmup tuning (non-prod): Owner: Neha (48h). Deliverable: tuned warmup policy, metrics dashboard.
- Short-term bridge (commercial): Owner: Ben (term sheet within 24h). Deliverable: credit term sheet + DocuSign link.
- Customer comms and executive note: Owner: Sergio (send consolidated email + schedule follow-up call).

Commercial term suggestion (draft — for Ben to refine):
- Credit covering the measured degradation window (08:42–09:03 PT) pro-rated by observed error/latency impact. Proposed ballpark: a one-time credit equivalent to 3 days of average spend for the dedicated pool (rounded). Rationale: preserves relationship while they validate the playbook; scope is prescriptive not an admission of wider SLA breach.

Questions for Ben: ok to propose the above ballpark or do we want to tighten based on per-token economics?

Marissa — I attached the current playbook draft (redwood_continuity_playbook_v1.pdf) with the sections I think we should prioritize in the canary.

Thanks — let’s aim to close commercial and run the canary by Monday.

Sergio Alvarez
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@atlas-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Consolidated commitment: playbook canary, tuning, and commercial bridge

Claire — thanks for validating details and for running traces with Ops. This note confirms what Redwood will commit to, and the near-term asks for Atlas to complete the canary validation.

What Redwood will deliver (committed):
- Evidence package: We delivered a sanitized logs bundle and scheduler traces (atlas_evidence_package.zip).
- Playbook canary: redwood_continuity_playbook_v1.pdf; Marissa will run a checklist in your non-prod and validate warmup behavior.
- Autoscaler tuning: Neha’s team will deliver a tuned warmup policy and monitoring dashboard within 48h after canary signoff.
- Commercial bridge: Ben will issue a DocuSign for a one-time credit reflecting the observed degradation window. Link: https://docusign.com/secure-link/ATLAS-CREDIT-78934 (attached term sheet: commercial_credit_term_sheet.pdf).

Immediate asks from Atlas:
- Confirm canary window: please propose a 2-hour non-prod window this week where traffic shape matches peak.
- Confirm that no tenant traffic was routed outside the dedicated pool during the 08:42–09:03 window (ops@ to confirm).

Proposed timeline:
- Today: Atlas to propose canary window. Redwood to finalize DocuSign and term sheet (Ben).
- 48h after canary signoff: deployment tuning and monitoring validated (Neha).
- 5 business days: staged roll if canary passes (Marissa / Atlas Ops).

We intend to treat this as a collaborative fast-path: minimal disruption, clear metrics, and a short commercial bridge so you can maintain availability while the playbook is validated.

If the above looks good I’ll:
1) send the DocuSign link to procurement (Ben),
2) schedule a 30-minute canary kickoff with your Ops (Marissa), and
3) follow up with a brief exec note summarizing the commitments.

Thanks again — we’ll stand by for the canary window.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachments: commercial_credit_term_sheet.pdf
